25 AUG 2026: ONE REQUEST, ACTIONED THE SAME DAY. Marriane asked whether the event detail page header could be a solid colour carrying the event details, instead of using the event poster as the background, so the text reads clearly - noting the poster already appears on the page. Confirmed with the user and implemented in components/events/event-detail/event-header.tsx: the full-bleed cover Image and its navy scrim are gone, replaced by a solid bg-navy panel with one soft mint bloom.

TWO THINGS THAT CAME OUT OF DOING IT.
1. KEEP: the old markup used bg-foreground, and --foreground INVERTS to white under .dark while --navy stays dark in both themes. The photograph was hiding that; removing it would have produced white text on a white panel in dark mode. The new panel uses bg-navy deliberately.
2. A WRONG TURN, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT REPEATED: EventPosters returns null when posters[] is empty and only 3 of 98 events have one, so it looked as though 20 events would lose their artwork, and a coverImage fallback was added to EventFeaturedPhoto. That was WRONG. app/(site)/events/[slug]/page.tsx already renders the cover whole and uncropped in an editorial frame at the top of the main column, unconditionally, for every event - which is precisely the "it's on the page itself" Marriane meant. The fallback duplicated it (the MYOB page rendered cover.webp twice) and was reverted. Check the page composition before adding a fallback for a component that looks conditional.
